newsitem.title: USA: Clinton telephones Netanyahu over helicopter crash.
newsitem.headline: Clinton telephones Netanyahu over helicopter crash.

text.p: President Bill Clinton telephoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday to express condolences over the mid-air collision of two military helicopters in which at least 70 soldiers died.
White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn said Clinton called Netanyahu from Air Force One as he flew from Washington for a visit to Georgia. They spoke for about five minutes.
"He just wanted to express his condolences on the helicopter crash yesterday. He feels for him and was thinking about him," Glynn said.
Netanyahu is to visit Washington on Feb. 13. Glynn said the president's call was strictly a condolence message.
The night-time collision of the two Sikorsky CH-53 transporters in northern Israel on their way to southern Lebanon was the worst military aviation disaster in the nearly 50 years of Israeli history.
